spanish: Ahora mismo yo ___ la cena para todos.
english: Right now I am making dinner for everyone.
explanation_or_example: Yo takes estoy, and -ar verbs form the gerund with -ando: estoy preparando. Está is for él, ella or usted.

spanish: ¿Con quién ___ tú por teléfono?
english: Who are you talking to on the phone?
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás, then the gerund: estás hablando. After estar the action needs -ando, never the infinitive.

spanish: Mi hermana ___ en el jardín en este momento.
english: My sister is working in the garden at the moment.
explanation_or_example: En este momento points to an action in progress, so estar plus the gerund: está trabajando. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Nosotros ___ la radio en la cocina.
english: We are listening to the radio in the kitchen.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros takes estamos: estamos escuchando. Están is for ellos or ustedes.

spanish: ¿Vosotros ___ para el examen de mañana?
english: Are you all studying for tomorrow's exam?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes estáis, matching the -áis ending: estáis estudiando. Estar needs the gerund, not the infinitive.

spanish: Los niños ___ en la piscina ahora.
english: The children are swimming in the pool now.
explanation_or_example: Los niños is ellos, so están nadando. Está only works with one person.

spanish: Ustedes ___ demasiado rápido por esta calle.
english: You are walking too fast along this street.
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes the same form as ellos: están caminando. Estáis goes with vosotros.

spanish: Perdone, ¿usted ___ a alguien?
english: Excuse me, are you waiting for someone?
explanation_or_example: Usted takes the third-person form: está esperando. Estás is for tú.

spanish: Yo ___ inglés a un grupo de adultos este mes.
english: I am teaching English to a group of adults this month.
explanation_or_example: Este mes frames a temporary activity that is still going on, so estoy enseñando. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Mira, el bebé ___ otra vez.
english: Look, the baby is crying again.
explanation_or_example: Mira points at something happening right now, so está llorando. Estar takes the gerund in -ando, not the infinitive.

spanish: Tú ___ muy bien esta canción.
english: You are singing this song very well.
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás, and the gerund of cantar is cantando. Cantado is the participle, which goes with haber.

spanish: Mis padres ___ el salón este fin de semana.
english: My parents are painting the living room this weekend.
explanation_or_example: Mis padres is ellos, so están, then the gerund: están pintando. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: Nosotras ___ un viaje a Portugal.
english: We are planning a trip to Portugal.
explanation_or_example: Nosotras takes estamos: estamos planeando. After estar comes the -ando form, not the infinitive.

spanish: ¿Qué ___ tú en el ordenador?
english: What are you looking for on the computer?
explanation_or_example: Tú pairs with estás, ending in -s like other tú forms: estás buscando. Está is for él, ella or usted.

spanish: El camarero ___ la mesa de la terraza.
english: The waiter is cleaning the table on the terrace.
explanation_or_example: El camarero is one person, so está limpiando. Están needs a plural subject.

spanish: Vosotras ___ muy bien en este partido.
english: You all are playing very well in this match.
explanation_or_example: Vosotras takes estáis: estáis jugando. Estar is followed by the gerund, never the infinitive.

spanish: Últimamente yo ___ mucho en bicicleta.
english: Lately I have been riding my bike a lot.
explanation_or_example: Últimamente frames a current, temporary habit, so estoy montando. Estar takes the -ando form, not the infinitive.

spanish: Ahora los estudiantes ___ sus respuestas.
english: Now the students are checking their answers.
explanation_or_example: Los estudiantes is ellos, so están revisando. Ser never forms the continuous; only estar does.

spanish: ¿Ustedes ___ bien en el hotel?
english: Are you resting well at the hotel?
explanation_or_example: Ustedes always takes están: están descansando. Estáis is for vosotros.

spanish: Mi abuelo ___ las plantas del balcón.
english: My grandfather is watering the plants on the balcony.
explanation_or_example: Mi abuelo is one person, so está, plus the gerund regando. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: Yo ___ con mis amigos por el parque.
english: I am taking a walk with my friends in the park.
explanation_or_example: Yo takes estoy, even with con mis amigos after it: estoy paseando. Estamos would need nosotros as the subject.

spanish: Esta semana nosotros ___ en un proyecto nuevo.
english: This week we are working on a new project.
explanation_or_example: Esta semana frames an activity still going on, so estamos plus the gerund: estamos trabajando. Trabajado is the participle, used with haber.

spanish: ¡Silencio! El profesor ___ la lección.
english: Quiet! The teacher is explaining the lesson.
explanation_or_example: Asking for silencio signals something happening right now, so está explicando. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Las chicas ___ salsa en la plaza.
english: The girls are dancing salsa in the square.
explanation_or_example: Las chicas is ellas, so están bailando. Está is singular.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ la tele o puedo apagarla?
english: Are you watching the TV or can I turn it off?
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás and the gerund mirando. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: El avión ___ en este momento.
english: The plane is landing at the moment.
explanation_or_example: El avión is singular, so está aterrizando. Están would need a plural subject.

spanish: Vosotros ___ la mudanza muy bien.
english: You all are organising the move very well.
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes estáis: estáis organizando. Están goes with ellos or ustedes.

spanish: La gente ___ en la calle para ver el desfile.
english: People are waiting in the street to see the parade.
explanation_or_example: La gente is grammatically singular in Spanish, so está esperando, even though English says people are.

spanish: ¿Usted ___ la cuenta con tarjeta?
english: Are you paying the bill by card?
explanation_or_example: Usted takes the third-person form: está pagando. Estás is the tú form.

spanish: Mi familia y yo ___ mucho de estas vacaciones.
english: My family and I are really enjoying this holiday.
explanation_or_example: Mi familia y yo includes yo, so the subject is nosotros: estamos disfrutando. Están would leave yo out.

spanish: Ahora mismo yo ___ un correo a mi jefa.
english: Right now I am writing an email to my boss.
explanation_or_example: Ahora mismo marks an action in progress, and -ir verbs take -iendo: estoy escribiendo. Escribir has no -ando form.

spanish: ¿Qué ___ tú? Huele muy bien.
english: What are you eating? It smells very good.
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás, and -er verbs take -iendo: estás comiendo. Estar needs the gerund, not the infinitive.

spanish: Mi hermano ___ en Berlín este año.
english: My brother is living in Berlin this year.
explanation_or_example: Este año frames a temporary situation, so estar plus the gerund: está viviendo. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Nosotros ___ mucho vocabulario nuevo.
english: We are learning a lot of new vocabulary.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros takes estamos: estamos aprendiendo. Están is for ellos or ustedes.

spanish: Los corredores ___ por el centro de la ciudad.
english: The runners are running through the city centre.
explanation_or_example: Los corredores is plural, so están corriendo. Está needs a singular subject.

spanish: ¿Vosotros ___ los deberes ahora?
english: Are you all doing your homework now?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes estáis, and hacer has a regular gerund: estáis haciendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: Shh, los niños ___ una película.
english: Shh, the children are watching a film.
explanation_or_example: Los niños is ellos, so están, and ver gives viendo: están viendo. After estar comes the gerund.

spanish: Mira por la ventana: ___ mucho.
english: Look out of the window: it is raining a lot.
explanation_or_example: Mira points at what is happening now, so está lloviendo. Weather in progress uses estar, never ser.

spanish: Usted ___ demasiado café, señor.
english: You are drinking too much coffee, sir.
explanation_or_example: Usted takes the third person: está bebiendo. Estás is the tú form.

spanish: Ustedes ___ la tienda muy temprano hoy.
english: You are opening the shop very early today.
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes están, like ellos: están abriendo. Estáis belongs to vosotros.

spanish: Yo ___ de casa ahora mismo, te llamo luego.
english: I am leaving home right now, I'll call you later.
explanation_or_example: Ahora mismo shows the action is under way, so estoy saliendo. Estar is followed by the gerund, not the infinitive.

spanish: Mi padre ___ la mesa para la cena.
english: My father is setting the table for dinner.
explanation_or_example: Mi padre is one person, so está poniendo. Poner has a regular gerund, poniendo.

spanish: Tú ___ fotos de todo el viaje.
english: You are uploading photos of the whole trip.
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás, and subir takes -iendo: estás subiendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: El equipo ___ el partido por dos goles.
english: The team is losing the match by two goals.
explanation_or_example: El equipo is one group and takes singular está: está perdiendo. Están would need a plural subject.

spanish: Nosotras ___ un piso con dos amigas.
english: We are sharing a flat with two friends.
explanation_or_example: Nosotras takes estamos, and -ir verbs take -iendo: estamos compartiendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: Vosotras ___ muchos mensajes hoy.
english: You all are getting a lot of messages today.
explanation_or_example: Vosotras takes estáis: estáis recibiendo. Están is for ellas or ustedes.

spanish: Mis tíos ___ su coche viejo.
english: My aunt and uncle are selling their old car.
explanation_or_example: Mis tíos is ellos, so están vendiendo. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Yo no ___ nada de lo que dice.
english: I am not understanding anything he is saying.
explanation_or_example: Yo takes estoy, and entender keeps its e in the gerund: estoy entendiendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: La abuela ___ las luces del salón.
english: Grandma is turning on the lights in the living room.
explanation_or_example: La abuela is one person, so está encendiendo. After estar comes the gerund, not the infinitive.

spanish: ¿Ustedes ___ el postre?
english: Are you choosing dessert?
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes están: están escogiendo. Estáis is for vosotros.

spanish: El paciente ___ mucho dolor hoy.
english: The patient is in a lot of pain today.
explanation_or_example: El paciente takes está: está sufriendo. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Los chicos ___ sobre fútbol otra vez.
english: The boys are arguing about football again.
explanation_or_example: Los chicos is ellos, so están discutiendo. Estar is followed by the gerund.

spanish: Yo ___ la cocina después de la cena.
english: I am sweeping the kitchen after dinner.
explanation_or_example: Yo takes estoy, and -er verbs take -iendo: estoy barriendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: Todo el mundo ___ la final en la tele.
english: Everyone is watching the final on TV.
explanation_or_example: Todo el mundo is grammatically singular, so está viendo, even though it means everyone.

spanish: Mi amiga y yo ___ una novela juntas.
english: My friend and I are writing a novel together.
explanation_or_example: Mi amiga y yo includes yo, so the subject is nosotras: estamos escribiendo. Están would leave yo out.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ un vestido para la boda?
english: Are you sewing a dress for the wedding?
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás, and coser takes -iendo: estás cosiendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: El profesor ___ el problema en la pizarra.
english: The teacher is solving the problem on the board.
explanation_or_example: El profesor takes está, and resolver keeps its o in the gerund: resolviendo. Ser never forms the continuous.

spanish: Vosotros ___ adónde ir de vacaciones.
english: You all are deciding where to go on holiday.
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes estáis: estáis decidiendo. Están is for ellos or ustedes.

spanish: La testigo ___ al ladrón a la policía.
english: The witness is describing the thief to the police.
explanation_or_example: La testigo is one person, so está, and describir takes -iendo: describiendo. Estar never takes the infinitive.

spanish: Mi perro ___ un hueso en el jardín.
english: My dog is hiding a bone in the garden.
explanation_or_example: Mi perro is singular, so está escondiendo. Están needs a plural subject.

spanish: Ahora mismo yo ___ el periódico.
english: Right now I am reading the newspaper.
explanation_or_example: Ahora mismo marks an action in progress. Leer has a vowel before the ending, so -iendo becomes -yendo: leyendo.

spanish: ¿Qué ___ tú? No te oigo bien.
english: What are you saying? I can't hear you well.
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás. Decir changes e to i in the gerund: diciendo, never deciendo.

spanish: El bebé ___ en su cuna.
english: The baby is sleeping in his cot.
explanation_or_example: El bebé takes está. Dormir changes o to u in the gerund: durmiendo.

spanish: Nosotros ___ una pizza por teléfono.
english: We are ordering a pizza by phone.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros takes estamos. Pedir changes e to i in the gerund: pidiendo, not pediendo.

spanish: Los camareros ___ la comida ahora.
english: The waiters are serving the food now.
explanation_or_example: Los camareros is ellos, so están. Servir changes e to i in the gerund: sirviendo.

spanish: ¿Vosotros ___ ese ruido?
english: Can you all hear that noise?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes estáis. Oír has a vowel before the ending, so the i becomes y: oyendo.

spanish: Mi madre ___ patatas para la tortilla.
english: My mother is frying potatoes for the omelette.
explanation_or_example: Mi madre takes está. Freír drops a vowel in the gerund: friendo.

spanish: ¿De qué ___ tú? ¿Qué es tan gracioso?
english: What are you laughing at? What's so funny?
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás. Reír drops the e in the gerund: riendo.

spanish: Ustedes ___ las mismas preguntas una y otra vez.
english: You are repeating the same questions over and over.
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes están. Repetir changes its last e to i in the gerund: repitiendo.

spanish: Usted ___ las instrucciones muy bien.
english: You are following the instructions very well.
explanation_or_example: Usted takes está. Seguir changes e to i in the gerund: siguiendo.

spanish: Ya ___ para allá, llego en diez minutos.
english: I'm on my way there already, I'll arrive in ten minutes.
explanation_or_example: Llego en diez minutos shows the trip is under way, so estoy. Ir has the irregular gerund yendo.

spanish: Los obreros ___ un puente nuevo sobre el río.
english: The workers are building a new bridge over the river.
explanation_or_example: Los obreros takes están. Construir puts a y in the gerund: construyendo.

spanish: Mira, las hojas ___ de los árboles.
english: Look, the leaves are falling from the trees.
explanation_or_example: Mira points at something happening now, so están cayendo. Caer has a vowel before the ending, so -iendo becomes -yendo.

spanish: Mi hijo ___ muy buenas notas este trimestre.
english: My son is getting very good marks this term.
explanation_or_example: Este trimestre frames something still going on, so está. Conseguir changes e to i in the gerund: consiguiendo.

spanish: La profesora ___ los exámenes en su despacho.
english: The teacher is marking the exams in her office.
explanation_or_example: La profesora takes está. Corregir changes e to i in the gerund: corrigiendo.

spanish: Cuidado, el agua ___ en la olla.
english: Careful, the water is boiling in the pot.
explanation_or_example: Cuidado warns about something happening now, so está. Hervir changes e to i in the gerund: hirviendo.

spanish: Tú me ___ otra vez, lo sé.
english: You are lying to me again, I know it.
explanation_or_example: Tú takes estás. Mentir changes e to i in the gerund: mintiendo.

spanish: Los atletas ___ por la medalla de oro.
english: The athletes are competing for the gold medal.
explanation_or_example: Los atletas takes están. Competir changes its last e to i in the gerund: compitiendo.

spanish: Vosotras ___ el regalo para Marta.
english: You all are choosing the present for Marta.
explanation_or_example: Vosotras takes estáis. Elegir changes e to i in the gerund: eligiendo.

spanish: Mis amigos me ___ un recuerdo de México.
english: My friends are bringing me a souvenir from Mexico.
explanation_or_example: Mis amigos takes están. Traer has a vowel before the ending, so -iendo becomes -yendo: trayendo.

spanish: Yo ___ mucho frío en esta casa.
english: I am feeling very cold in this house.
explanation_or_example: Yo takes estoy. Sentir changes e to i in the gerund: sintiendo.

spanish: El ladrón ___ de la policía por los tejados.
english: The thief is fleeing from the police across the rooftops.
explanation_or_example: El ladrón takes está. Huir puts a y in the gerund: huyendo.

spanish: Los gatos ___ al sol.
english: The cats are sleeping in the sun.
explanation_or_example: Los gatos is plural, so están. Dormir changes o to u in the gerund: durmiendo.

spanish: Las plantas ___ por falta de agua.
english: The plants are dying from lack of water.
explanation_or_example: Las plantas takes están. Morir changes o to u in the gerund: muriendo.

spanish: ¿Usted ___ bien lo que digo?
english: Can you hear what I'm saying properly?
explanation_or_example: Usted takes está. Oír turns the i of the ending into y: oyendo.

spanish: Nosotros ___ el río hasta el pueblo.
english: We are following the river to the village.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros takes estamos. Seguir changes e to i in the gerund: siguiendo.

spanish: La tormenta ___ muchos árboles del parque.
english: The storm is destroying a lot of trees in the park.
explanation_or_example: La tormenta takes está. Destruir puts a y in the gerund: destruyendo.

spanish: La enfermera ___ la temperatura a los pacientes.
english: The nurse is taking the patients' temperature.
explanation_or_example: La enfermera takes está. Medir changes e to i in the gerund: midiendo.

spanish: ¿Qué ___ vosotros en el club de lectura?
english: What are you all reading in the book club?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes estáis. Leer has a vowel before the ending, so the gerund is leyendo.

spanish: El jefe ___ a varios empleados.
english: The boss is firing several employees.
explanation_or_example: El jefe takes está. Despedir changes its last e to i in the gerund: despidiendo.

spanish: ¿El periódico? Estoy ___ en el sofá.
english: The newspaper? I am reading it on the sofa.
explanation_or_example: Estoy is already in the sentence, so lo attaches to the gerund: leyéndolo. Adding a pronoun needs a written accent.

spanish: ¿La carta? Mi madre está ___ en la cocina.
english: The letter? My mother is writing it in the kitchen.
explanation_or_example: With está already in place, la attaches to the end of the gerund: escribiéndola. A pronoun never goes between estar and the gerund.

spanish: Ahora mismo estoy ___ con agua fría.
english: Right now I am having a shower with cold water.
explanation_or_example: Estoy is already there, so me attaches to the gerund: duchándome. The attached pronoun needs a written accent.

spanish: Los niños están ___ para ir al colegio.
english: The children are getting dressed for school.
explanation_or_example: Están is already there, so se attaches to the gerund: vistiéndose. Vestir changes e to i, and the accent keeps the stress.

spanish: ¿Las fotos? Estamos ___ ahora.
english: The photos? We are looking at them now.
explanation_or_example: Estamos is already there, so las attaches to the gerund: mirándolas. A pronoun never goes between estar and the gerund.

spanish: ¿Tu coche? Mi hermano está ___ en el garaje.
english: Your car? My brother is fixing it in the garage.
explanation_or_example: Está is already there, so lo attaches to the gerund: arreglándolo. The written accent keeps the stress on the same syllable.

spanish: Ana, ¿estás ___ en la fiesta?
english: Ana, are you having fun at the party?
explanation_or_example: Estás is already there, so te attaches to the gerund. Divertir changes e to i in the gerund: divirtiéndote.

spanish: ¿El regalo? Estoy ___ a mi hermana ahora.
english: The present? I am giving it to my sister now.
explanation_or_example: Estoy is already there, so se and lo attach to the gerund in that order: dándoselo. Two attached pronouns always need the accent.

spanish: ¿La verdad? El testigo está ___ al juez.
english: The truth? The witness is telling it to the judge.
explanation_or_example: Está is already there, so se and la attach to the gerund: diciéndosela. Two attached pronouns need a written accent.

spanish: Mis padres están ___ en el sofá.
english: My parents are relaxing on the sofa.
explanation_or_example: Están is already there, so se attaches to the gerund: relajándose. The accent keeps the stress on the same syllable.

spanish: ¿Los platos? Vosotros estáis ___ muy rápido.
english: The dishes? You all are washing them very fast.
explanation_or_example: Estáis is already there, so los attaches to the gerund: lavándolos. A pronoun never goes between estar and the gerund.

spanish: ¿La cena? Estamos ___ para todos.
english: Dinner? We are making it for everyone.
explanation_or_example: Estamos is already there, so la attaches to the gerund: preparándola. The attached pronoun needs a written accent.

spanish: ¿Las instrucciones? Ustedes están ___ con mucha atención.
english: The instructions? You are reading them very carefully.
explanation_or_example: Están is already there, so las attaches to the gerund: leyéndolas. A pronoun never goes between estar and the gerund.

spanish: El perro está ___ al sol en la terraza.
english: The dog is drying off in the sun on the terrace.
explanation_or_example: Está is already there, so se attaches to the gerund: secándose. The attached pronoun needs a written accent.

spanish: ¿El problema? La profesora está ___ a los alumnos paso a paso.
english: The problem? The teacher is explaining it to the students step by step.
explanation_or_example: Está is already there, so se and lo attach to the gerund: explicándoselo. Two attached pronouns always need the accent.

spanish: ¿El libro? Yo lo ___ ahora mismo.
english: The book? I'm reading it right now.
explanation_or_example: Lo is already before the blank, so estoy and the gerund follow on their own: estoy leyendo. The pronoun can't appear twice.

spanish: Mi hermana se ___ el pelo en el baño.
english: My sister is drying her hair in the bathroom.
explanation_or_example: Se is already before the blank, so está secando follows without another pronoun. Secándose would repeat se.

spanish: ¿Las llaves? Nosotros las ___ por toda la casa.
english: The keys? We are looking for them all over the house.
explanation_or_example: Las is already before the blank, so estamos buscando follows on its own. Buscándolas would say las twice.

spanish: Tranquila, yo te ___ con atención.
english: Don't worry, I am listening to you carefully.
explanation_or_example: Te is already before the blank, so estoy escuchando follows on its own. Escuchándote would say te twice.

spanish: ¿La película? Los niños la ___ en el salón.
english: The film? The children are watching it in the living room.
explanation_or_example: La is already before the blank, so están viendo follows on its own. Viéndola would repeat la.

spanish: Vosotros os ___ muchísimo en la fiesta, ¿verdad?
english: You all are having a great time at the party, aren't you?
explanation_or_example: Os is already before the blank, so estáis divirtiendo follows on its own. Divertir changes e to i in the gerund.

spanish: ¿Usted me ___ bien desde ahí?
english: Can you hear me properly from there?
explanation_or_example: Me is already before the blank, so está oyendo follows on its own. Oyéndome would say me twice.

spanish: Yo me ___ para la entrevista de trabajo.
english: I am getting ready for the job interview.
explanation_or_example: Me is already before the blank, so estoy preparando follows on its own. Preparándome would repeat me.

spanish: ¿El informe? Mi jefe me lo ___ ahora mismo.
english: The report? My boss is asking me for it right now.
explanation_or_example: Me lo is already before the blank, so está pidiendo follows on its own. Pedir changes e to i in the gerund.

spanish: Tú se lo ___ a todo el mundo.
english: You are telling it to everyone.
explanation_or_example: Se lo is already before the blank, so estás contando follows on its own. Contándoselo would say se lo twice.

spanish: Los invitados se ___ ya.
english: The guests are saying goodbye now.
explanation_or_example: Se is already before the blank, so están despidiendo follows on its own. Despedir changes e to i in the gerund.

spanish: ¿La casa? Mis abuelos la ___ este año.
english: The house? My grandparents are selling it this year.
explanation_or_example: La is already before the blank, so están vendiendo follows on its own. Vendiéndola would repeat la.

spanish: Ustedes se ___ mucho con este calor.
english: You are complaining a lot in this heat.
explanation_or_example: Se is already before the blank, so están quejando follows on its own. Quejándose would say se twice.

spanish: Nosotras nos ___ para salir.
english: We are getting ready to go out.
explanation_or_example: Nos is already before the blank, so estamos arreglando follows on its own. Arreglándonos would repeat nos.

spanish: ¿Los deberes? Tú los ___ sin ganas.
english: Your homework? You are doing it half-heartedly.
explanation_or_example: Los is already before the blank, so estás haciendo follows on its own. Haciéndolos would say los twice.

spanish: Me encanta ___ en el mar en verano.
english: I love swimming in the sea in summer.
explanation_or_example: After me encanta the activity is an infinitive: nadar. English uses -ing here, but Spanish never uses the gerund.
